interviewQuestions.question: Compare bus, crossbar, and mesh interconnects. Why do large multicore chips use a mesh/NoC?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
⭐ **Q: Compare bus, crossbar, and mesh interconnects. Why do large chips use mesh/NoC?**

A **bus** is simplest — every core shares one set of wires, why snooping coherence relies on it — but bandwidth is fixed, becoming a contention point; tops out at a handful of cores.

A **crossbar** gives every core a dedicated path to every other, eliminating contention, but costs roughly N² in switching hardware — impractical past dozens of cores.

A **mesh (NoC)** connects each core to its neighbors only, routing longer messages hop-by-hop. Cost grows roughly linearly — why large chips use mesh.

**Testing:** explaining *why* each breaks down, not just naming a winner.
